_readme: What each engineering calculator checks and what it leaves unverified, shown under every result. Written from what the code in engine.js does, and re-checked when a calculator changes. A calculator without an entry here shows the default for its method basis.

checked: The arithmetic of the published formula for the values you entered, in the units shown.
notChecked: That the inputs suit your application. Take ratings, resistances and constants from the manufacturer data sheet or project specification.

checked: The arithmetic of the published formula for the values you entered.
notChecked: The constants and size lists against the licensed edition of the standard.
Any check outside the formula shown (see the notes).

checked: The arithmetic of the simplified model for the values you entered.
notChecked: Whether the simplifying assumptions listed on this page hold for your case.
Any standard, manufacturer or site data. Treat the result as an estimate and confirm it by a further engineering check.

checked: Smallest IEC 60228 size that keeps voltage drop within the limit you set, with resistance at the full-load conductor temperature.
notChecked: Current-carrying capacity (no ampacity table is embedded).
Installation method, grouping, ambient and soil correction.
Short-circuit withstand and protective-device coordination.
Cable manufacturer AC resistance and reactance (a constant reactance is assumed).

checked: Iz = tabulated rating you enter × temperature factor × grouping factor × other factor.
Rule Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz for the chosen basis (1.25 × Ib for the NEC-style continuous case).
notChecked: The temperature factor is a heat-balance approximation, not the factor tabulated in the wiring standard.
The tabulated rating, grouping factor and installation method are yours to take from the data sheet or licensed standard.
Harmonics, soil thermal resistivity, voltage drop and short-circuit withstand.

checked: Vd from the R and X per km you enter, current, length, power factor and parallel conductors.
notChecked: Whether the cable carries the current (ampacity).
The permitted drop for your circuit type and edition of the wiring rules.
Mutual effects between parallel conductors and unbalanced loads.

checked: AC voltage drop from conductor material, size, length and temperature, with the reactance you enter, for lagging or leading load.
notChecked: Skin and proximity effect (they matter above about 150 mm²).
Ampacity, installation method and grouping.
Manufacturer AC resistance and reactance for the real cable.
The permitted drop for your circuit type.

checked: Longest run that stays within the drop limit for the R and X you enter.
notChecked: Ampacity and short-circuit withstand.
Earth-fault loop impedance and disconnection time at that length.

checked: Minimum conductor area S = I√t / k with the built-in adiabatic k values.
notChecked: The k values against the current edition of the standard (initial and final temperatures, size range, insulation).
The real clearing time at the fault level: take it from the protective-device curve.
Let-through energy of the breaker, and the withstand of screens and armour.

checked: Number of equal cable sets needed so that each carries no more than Iz × k.
notChecked: Whether the sets really share current equally (length, route, spacing, termination).
Voltage drop, grouping and short-circuit withstand of the sets.

checked: Smallest standard rating at or above the current × margin, and that it does not exceed the cable capacity you enter.
notChecked: Breaking capacity against the prospective fault level.
Trip curve, instantaneous pick-up and let-through energy.
Selectivity with upstream and downstream devices.

checked: Terminal three-phase fault current from kVA, voltage and transformer impedance, with an infinite source.
notChecked: Source (utility) impedance and cable impedance, so the value is an upper bound.
Minimum fault level, needed for protection to operate.
Motor contribution and the IEC 60909 voltage factor.

checked: Three-phase, line-to-line and line-to-earth bolted-fault currents from Z1, Z0 and voltage.
notChecked: Arc resistance and the angle of the impedances (they are combined as magnitudes).
Z2 = Z1 is assumed.
Maximum versus minimum fault-level cases and the IEC 60909 factors.

checked: Conversion between fault current and fault level at the voltage you enter.
notChecked: Where the fault level comes from: the source data and the maximum or minimum case are yours to confirm.

checked: Zs = Ze + R1 + R2, the earth-fault current at U0 and the Zs needed for the device operating current you enter.
notChecked: The disconnection time and the permitted Zs from your wiring rules.
The device trip characteristic, conductor temperature and reactance.
Ze is yours to obtain from the supply authority or by measurement.

checked: Single-rod resistance from soil resistivity, rod length and diameter.
notChecked: Measured soil resistivity, layering and seasonal variation.
Neighbouring electrodes, and step and touch voltage.

checked: Combined resistance Rn = R1 / (n × u) for the number of rods and the utilisation factor you enter.
notChecked: The utilisation factor is yours: it depends on rod spacing and soil, and is not calculated here.
Measured soil resistivity and seasonal variation.
Step and touch voltage.

checked: Grid resistance from soil resistivity, area and conductor length (Laurent-Niemann form).
notChecked: Burial depth refinement, measured resistivity and layered soil.
Step and touch voltage, ground potential rise and a full earthing study.

checked: Resistor value for the earth-fault current you choose, its power and energy for the stated time.
notChecked: Source impedance and the relay settings.
The resistor's short-time and thermal rating from the manufacturer.

checked: Smallest standard kVA at or above the load, growth and loading target.
notChecked: Harmonics (K-rating), motor starting and ambient temperature.
Impedance, losses and cooling class: take them from the transformer data sheet.

checked: Starting current and torque ratios for DOL, star-delta and auto-transformer starting.
notChecked: Supply voltage sag during the start.
The motor's real locked-rotor current and torque curve.

checked: Voltage dip at the bus from motor starting kVA and source fault level.
notChecked: Starting power factor and the true impedance angles.
The effect on other loads on the bus.

checked: Fill percentage against the 53 / 31 / 40% NEC-style limits.
notChecked: Whether that rule applies in your code (it is not a universal IEC or IS rule).
Pulling tension, bends, run length and cable derating inside the conduit.

checked: Voltage regulation from the resistance, reactance, load and power factor entered.
notChecked: The impedance and loss figures: take them from the test certificate or data sheet.

checked: Standard kVA at or above the load, with the margin entered.
notChecked: Motor starting, transient voltage and frequency dip, harmonics and altitude or temperature derating.
